FINDING_ID: ROUND2_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.91  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.86  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`FailureHandler.detect_failure()` accepts and processes responses from inactive/excluded models, which can silently contaminate manager state after exclusion.** `FailureHandler` maintains `_active_models`, and `DynamicManager.get_live_models()` respects it for future allocation, but `process_round()` still iterates over every entry in caller-supplied `responses` and passes each to `detect_failure()` and `get_recovery()` without checking membership in `active_models`. Because `detect_failure()` also appends to `_perf_history` unconditionally, a previously excluded model can keep influencing underperformance history and failure history if the orchestrator mistakenly includes stale responses. This is a cross-area integrity gap: Area 6 tracks active membership, Area 1 records failures, and orchestration trusts external input instead of enforcing the active-set invariant. A robust implementation should reject or ignore responses for inactive models before any state mutation.  

FINDING_ID: ROUND2_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.83  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager.process_round()` never validates that `responses[*].model_id` matches the dictionary key, enabling identity spoofing and cross-model state corruption.** The method loops as `for model_id, response in responses.items():` but all failure logic uses `response.model_id`, not the map key. If the caller supplies `responses = {"m1": ModelResponse(model_id="m2", ...)}`, then failures, performance history, and emitted events are attributed to `m2` while the outer map slot implies `m1`. This can desynchronise failure histories, active-model membership, and audit logs. Prior findings noted missing integrity checks in broad terms, but this concrete aliasing bug is a sharper mechanism: the public API contains two model identity channels and never enforces equality. The manager should assert `response.model_id == model_id` for every entry before proceeding.  

FINDING_ID: ROUND2_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.84  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager.process_round()` accepts findings from unknown or inactive models and folds them directly into convergence and fingerprint updates.** There is no validation that each `Finding.model_id` belongs to the configured pool, is currently active, or even appears in `responses`. As a result, a malformed caller can inject arbitrary findings from non-existent model IDs into `ConvergenceDetector.add_round_findings()`, altering convergence, diminishing-returns, and novelty metrics. Separately, `update_fingerprints()` groups findings by `model_id` and only updates active known models, so the injected findings affect global metrics without corresponding per-model accountability. This is a cross-cutting trust-boundary flaw: the manager treats caller-supplied findings as authoritative despite having enough local state to validate provenance.  

FINDING_ID: ROUND2_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.79  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **Missing responses are treated as success-by-omission.** In `process_round()`, only models present in `responses.items()` are examined for failure, and only those models get `RoleAssignment.record_failure(...)` entries for the round. Any active model omitted from `responses` incurs no EMPTY/TIMEOUT failure, no underperformance update, and no failure-history update at all. That means the easiest way for a caller/orchestrator bug to avoid penalties is to omit the response entirely instead of reporting an empty or timed-out result. This is distinct from the earlier observation that `tasks` and allocation are not tied into failure handling: even without allocation awareness, the manager knows the active model set and can detect absent responses relative to it. Current behavior biases histories and recovery decisions by turning absence into invisibility.  

FINDING_ID: ROUND2_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.72  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The API never enforces round-index consistency between `DynamicManager`, `ModelResponse`, and `Finding`.** `process_round()` computes `round_idx = self.fsm.current_round` and stores results under that index, but it never checks that every `response.round_idx` and `finding.round_idx` equals that same value. This allows delayed, replayed, or future-tagged artifacts to be ingested into the wrong round. Because convergence caches, per-round duration, failure history, and audit state are keyed by the manager’s round index rather than each object’s embedded index, the system can silently absorb cross-round contamination while leaving apparently plausible metadata behind. This is an integrity flaw independent of the already-reported duplicate-index bug: even if round numbering were fixed, the manager still trusts inconsistent per-object round tags.  

FINDING_ID: ROUND2_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.77  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager.__init__()` permits construction with an empty model pool to fail via an unhandled `ValueError` from `RoleAssignment.assign()`, rather than validating the public API boundary itself.** The top-level manager is the user-facing abstraction, yet it delegates emptiness checking to a lower layer and provides no contextual error or dedicated invariant check. This is not just style: several later assumptions (`FailureHandler`, fingerprint stores, PM existence) require a non-empty pool, so the manager should reject invalid construction explicitly and consistently. As written, the class exposes a leaky internal precondition instead of a manager-level contract.  

FINDING_ID: ROUND2_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.75  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`ManagerEventStream.emit()` is not exception-safe: a failing callback can prevent buffering/logging of events and abort manager execution mid-update.** The method appends to `_buffer` and `_all_events` before invoking the callback, which preserves already-emitted events, but any callback exception propagates straight through the manager. Since `DynamicManager.process_round()` emits events inline during processing, a consumer-side callback bug can interrupt failure handling, convergence updates, or fingerprint updates and leave the manager in a partially mutated state. This is a cross-cutting orchestration hazard: observability is allowed to become a control-path failure source. A serious manager should either isolate callback failures or document them as hard-fail semantics; current code does neither.  

FINDING_ID: ROUND2_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION: 0.68  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`ConvergenceDetector._compute_equivalence_classes()` generates unstable `class_id` values that are order-dependent and unsuitable for any longitudinal identity use.** Class IDs are assigned as `ec_{idx}` based on iteration order over the transient `clusters` dict produced by union-find roots. Because root selection depends on union order and input order, semantically identical finding sets can receive different class IDs across recomputation or different insertion orders. The current module mostly treats class IDs as ephemeral, but the type and docstring imply persistent equivalence-class identity. This becomes a latent bug if any caller stores or compares `class_id` across rounds. The safer design is to document IDs as ephemeral or derive stable IDs from canonical member content.  

FINDING_ID: ROUND2_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.67  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.71  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The manager emits `ROUND_COMPLETE` at the start of `process_round()` and again after fingerprint updates, but never emits `ROUND_START`, making the event protocol semantically inconsistent.** The first emission says “Processing round ...” before any processing has happened; later a second `ROUND_COMPLETE` event is used as a fingerprint-update notification. Downstream consumers therefore cannot rely on event names to reconstruct lifecycle order, and a naïve listener may interpret the round as complete before failures and convergence have even been computed. This is deeper than missing recovery events: the existing progress events themselves do not form a coherent state machine. Event taxonomy should distinguish round-begin, round-processed, and fingerprint-updated phases explicitly.  

FINDING_ID: ROUND2_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.66  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **No validation prevents NaN or infinite numeric fields in core dataclasses, allowing silent propagation of non-finite values through scoring and decision logic.** `CapabilityFingerprint`, `ModelSpec`, `Task`, `Finding`, and `ModelResponse` accept arbitrary floats; `DynamicManagementConfig.__post_init__()` only validates a few fields. If a caller supplies `nan` severity, `inf` token demand, or `nan` response time, NumPy operations and comparisons can yield silent misbehavior: sort keys become unstable, objective values can become `nan`, feasibility checks may fail to trigger, and convergence metrics can collapse unpredictably. This is a broad input-sanitisation gap not covered by earlier bounded-threshold observations, because it affects runtime artifacts as well as config. The module needs finite-value validation on all externally supplied numeric data.  

FINDING_ID: ROUND2_F011  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION: 0.62  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`RoleAssignment.reassign()` accepts a `round_idx` parameter but never uses it, indicating the advertised round-aware reassignment policy is not actually indexed by round.** The docstring claims the current round is part of the decision context, yet the implementation applies only aggregate failure-history means. This means ancient failures are weighted forever and there is no mechanism for recency-sensitive reassignment despite the API suggesting one. The bug is not merely cosmetic: carrying an unused round index hides that the reassignment policy has no temporal decay or round-local behavior. Either remove the parameter or implement genuinely round-aware history weighting.  

FINDING_ID: ROUND2_F012  
SEVERITY: 0.55  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION: 0.60  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The public design claim “Every active model gets work matched to its demonstrated capability” is unsupported by the implementation and contradicted at the API boundary.** `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` passes live fingerprints into `LoadBalancer`, but `LoadBalancer` ignores fingerprints entirely and allocates solely by load and role admissibility. A stronger version of this disconnect was already found for adaptive routing in general; the missed point here is that the manager’s own method-level contract explicitly promises per-model capability matching, which is false even if role reassignment were fixed. This is a documentation/API truthfulness defect that can mislead integrators into assuming task-capability matching exists when it does not.
